selection_firewall.candidate_origin: MC08 exchange/metathesis class-gap search using kinetics-first to independent-barrier pairing by reaction identity and mechanistic representation before any residual, chi, or ChemSA calculation

classification_basis: The elementary event exchanges the halide bound to methyl through bimolecular nucleophilic substitution and therefore belongs to the frozen MC08 exchange/metathesis class.
The physical family is distinct from the frozen gas-phase H3 exchange family and is not an isotopologue or same-family replicate.
This trail does not supersede the separately held chloride/methyl-chloride identity-SN2 trail.

theory_source.title: Benchmark ab Initio Characterization of the Complex Potential Energy Surface of the Cl- + CH3I Reaction
theory_source.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
theory_source.purpose: benchmark stationary-point structures and classical/adiabatic relative energies for the multi-path Cl- + CH3I potential-energy surface
theory_source.method: focal-point analysis: CCSD(T)/CBS + deltaCCSDT + deltaCCSDT(Q) + core correlation; adiabatic values add CCSD(T)-F12b/aug-cc-pVTZ zero-point-energy corrections
theory_source.method_selection_provenance: The paper specifies a benchmark coupled-cluster/focal-point hierarchy and reports a broad stationary-point map. It discusses prior crossed-beam dynamics literature but does not disclose fitting the benchmark stationary energies to the selected 2001 thermal rate coefficient. No energy or method variant is selected here by observed-rate residual.

derived_central_barrier_above_precomplex.calculation: WaldenTS minus PreMIN using the source-tabulated benchmark relative energies

barrier_quantity.type: benchmark intrinsic potential-energy-surface stationary-point energies; classical values are electronic-energy focal-point results and adiabatic values add zero-point-energy corrections
barrier_quantity.submerged_saddle_note: WaldenTS is below the separated-reactant asymptote in both benchmark profiles, so its negative relative energy must not be treated as a negative single-step thermal activation free energy.

primary_source.authors: Shuji Kato, Gustavo E. Davico, Hack Sung Lee, Charles H. DePuy, Veronica M. Bierbaum
primary_source.title: Deuterium kinetic isotope effects in gas phase SN2 reactions

observed_rate_coefficient.absolute_systematic_uncertainty_note: approximately 20 percent according to the source table note

condition_mapping.species_and_charge_state: MATCHED: Cl- + CH3I reactants and CH3Cl + I- products
condition_mapping.experimental_state_point: 300 K, helium carrier, approximately 0.5 Torr flow-tube pressure
condition_mapping.theory_state_definition: intrinsic classical and zero-point-corrected adiabatic PES energies, not assigned a 300 K thermal label
condition_mapping.mapping_rule: The observed thermal rate is compared only to the correctly typed network PES representation. The intrinsic energies are not relabelled as 300 K DeltaG_dagger or as a thermal activation enthalpy.

independence_basis: The selected direct kinetic measurement was published in 2001, sixteen years before the 2017 benchmark PES study.
The selected experiment and benchmark computation come from independent research groups and experimental/theoretical lineages.
The 2017 benchmark protocol is a pre-specified coupled-cluster focal-point hierarchy across many stationary points; no same-target fitting to the selected 2001 thermal rate is disclosed.
No residual, chi value, reaction efficiency, isotope effect, or expected ChemSA agreement was used to choose this candidate or any theory variant.
representation_basis: The benchmark PES contains an entrance ion-dipole complex, submerged Walden saddle, exit complex, and additional higher-energy pathways. The thermal rate therefore cannot be represented honestly by a lone separated-reactant scalar barrier.
quarantined_evidence: The source-reported inverse kinetic isotope effect is not used to select or promote the candidate.
The source-reported reaction efficiency is not used to select or promote the candidate.
Any agreement between prior dynamics calculations and crossed-beam experiments discussed by the 2017 paper is not used to select the benchmark barrier profile.
No predicted/observed residual, chi value, or expected ChemSA agreement may vote on candidate selection or promotion.
